result.title: A Topological Signature of Learning under Noisy Labels
result.summary: How does noisy supervision change the representations learned by a neural network? Training accuracy measures agreement with training labels but provides little information about representation geometry. We use persistent homology to track loop structure across distance thresholds in neural activations. Experiments span image classification, text classification, and modular arithmetic. On a fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe, equally sized clean-label and corrupted-label subsets show no detectable persistence difference at epoch 10, whereas corrupted-label subsets have higher persistence at epoch 50. The contrast survives uniform-scale controls, even though predictions match the assigned noisy labels for only 7-11% of corrupted probe examples at that checkpoint. Normalisation preserves the crossover between clean and noisy training trajectories on CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, whereas CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 shows no crossover under any of the five evaluated constructions. In a separate noise-rate calibration comparison across five pipelines, mean activation norm achieves a higher mean in-sample R2 than raw persistence (0.936 versus 0.908). These findings show that noisy supervision leaves a measurable geometric signature even when agreement with corrupted labels is low. Comparing persistence under scale controls with label-fitting measurements offers a way to study how representations respond to label corruption beyond what training accuracy reveals.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用持续同调（persistent homology）追踪神经网络激活在不同距离阈值下的环结构，在图像分类、文本分类和模算术任务上比较干净标签与噪声标签训练所产生表示几何的差异，并报告了不同训练阶段的持续性交叉现象及尺度控制下的对照结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但其用拓扑工具刻画内部表示几何、并区分监督信号被污染时表示结构如何变化，可能为分析 latent 推理状态的几何结构与轨迹监督质量提供可供核查的诊断线索。
